name: Layer 7 Cortical Interface
description: Layer 7 is a thin, flexible sheet of electrodes placed on the surface of the brain. The electrodes measure small voltage changes produced by nearby neural activity. Its surface position differs from an array of needles that penetrates the cortex. The sheet must work with recording electronics and other equipment; it is not a complete computer-control system by itself.

The immediate task to understand is cortical recording and monitoring around neurosurgical care. A high-density array can collect signals from many closely spaced locations, which may help researchers or clinicians study activity over the exposed cortex. Separately, the company aims to use cortical signals in an assistive brain-computer interface. That larger task also requires reliable decoding, a practical implant system and evidence that a person can use it over time.

For this coursework, choose the exact product before collecting a market size or business story. The temporary Layer 7-T electrode and a future long-term assistive BCI have different users, clinical evidence, costs and buyers. Treating them as one finished product would make all five sections difficult to support.
stage: A temporary electrode component has a 2025 FDA 510(k) record for use of less than 30 days. The company’s broader assistive BCI remains a separate investigational development. The clearest report would study the marketed component and explain the larger platform as its development context.
clinical_evidence: The reviewed FDA record, K242618 (2025), covers Layer 7-T cortical electrodes used with recording, monitoring and stimulation equipment for temporary use of less than 30 days. It does not establish approval of a permanent implant that restores computer control. The company separately describes the broader BCI system as investigational. This boundary changes the need, evidence and reimbursement sections.
summary: Interesting BCI technology, but first decide whether the report concerns the temporary electrode or the broader platform. Payment and exact-product IP are the main information gaps.
london_summary: No London Layer 7-T user was verified. The useful product-origin lead is overseas.

name: RNS System
description: The RNS System is an implanted treatment for selected people with drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Electrodes are placed at or near one or two identified seizure sources. They connect to a neurostimulator implanted in the skull. The system records local brain electrical activity and looks for patterns that the treating team has programmed it to detect.

When a programmed pattern is detected, the device delivers a short electrical stimulation. This is the meaning of responsive or closed-loop treatment: the recorded signal affects when stimulation is delivered. It does not need to wait for a person to press a button. The clinician still sets and adjusts the detection and stimulation parameters; the device does not independently decide every aspect of epilepsy care.

Recorded data also give the clinical team a view of activity between appointments. This makes the product both a treatment and a source of long-term intracranial recordings. The case can therefore explain why sensing, stimulation, follow-up and data review have to work together. It should also explain the surgical and monitoring burden and the alternatives available to the same patients.
stage: This is a marketed US implant, with original PMA approval in 2013 and a substantial clinical history. The selected case should remain focal epilepsy. Investigational generalized-epilepsy work is a separate indication, not evidence that the original label covers every epilepsy type.
clinical_evidence: The original 2013 PMA concerns adults with drug-resistant focal/partial-onset seizures, with no more than two localized foci and other label criteria. In the 191-person randomized study, seizure frequency fell 37.9% with active stimulation versus 17.3% with sham during the blinded evaluation. The nine-year study reports a 75% median reduction, but that later figure comes from open-label follow-up, not another nine-year randomized comparison. A July 2026 company FDA update did not establish approval for generalized epilepsy.
summary: One of the clearer choices for public research: trials, an early patent, a detailed prospectus and an economic model are already identified. Early financing still needs careful extraction.
london_summary: No exact RNS user in London was verified. Use product-specific US evidence rather than presenting a general London epilepsy specialist as an RNS contact.

name: Rapid Response EEG / Clarity
description: Ceribell is a bedside EEG system designed to make a brain recording available quickly in emergency and intensive care settings. The clinical problem is that a patient may have seizures without obvious convulsions, while a conventional EEG setup and specialist review take time. A rapidly applied scalp headband and portable recorder provide an earlier view of electrical activity.

There are several parts to keep separate. The headband and recorder acquire EEG. The Brain Stethoscope feature converts aspects of the signal into sound. Clarity-family software analyses seizure-related patterns and can assist assessment of seizure burden. These features have different development and clearance histories; evidence for one version does not automatically establish the performance of another.

The useful entrepreneurship story is the whole hospital workflow: who can put the headband on, how quickly a usable recording becomes available, how a clinician interprets it, and when conventional EEG is still needed. Reduced coverage and software assistance do not make it a complete substitute for every conventional EEG examination. Faster recording also does not by itself prove better survival or lower costs; those require their own evidence.
stage: Ceribell is a commercial EEG platform. The selected FDA document, K223504, concerns a later Status Epilepticus Monitor configuration. A report should trace the first hardware and sound-based system separately from subsequent AI/software versions.
clinical_evidence: The DECIDE prospective observational study enrolled 181 critically ill patients and assessed workflow and physician decisions. It supports a rapid-access story, not a randomized mortality benefit. A separate 38-patient emergency-care pilot contained only one NCSE case: its nominal 100% sensitivity has a very wide confidence interval. K223504 reviews the Ceribell Status Epilepticus Monitor, so it should not be silently treated as the original headband clearance or every later Clarity version.
summary: Useful public clinical and economic sources exist. The task is to choose the hardware/software version and reconstruct its early licensing and funding history.
london_summary: No exact Ceribell user in London was verified. A general London EEG researcher is not enough to support a product-specific contact recommendation.

contacts.limits: He has a commercial connection to the company. A developer’s account should be checked against patents, trials and payer records; it does not establish London use.

name: SAINT
description: SAINT combines individualized brain targeting with an intensive course of transcranial magnetic stimulation for depression. A functional MRI scan is used to help choose a cortical target for the individual patient. A stimulation coil is then positioned using the treatment system’s targeting/navigation process.

The coil produces changing magnetic fields that induce electrical activity in the brain. SAINT uses an accelerated intermittent theta-burst schedule: multiple sessions are delivered each day over five days, rather than spreading the whole course over many weeks. The commercial product therefore includes software, a targeting workflow and compatible stimulation/navigation hardware.

Personalized targeting and accelerated delivery are the main features to investigate. The scan informs where treatment is given; it is not a live EEG feedback loop that decides each pulse. The business case also depends on practical delivery: access to MRI, staff time across an intensive day, repeat or continuation treatment, and whether a payer covers the full pathway. A clinic offering generic accelerated TMS is not automatically using the licensed Magnus SAINT system.
stage: The Magnus system received FDA clearance in 2022, and manufacturer material records commercialization in 2024. It is beyond an academic prototype, but the early small trial and later clinical delivery should be distinguished. No exact licensed London delivery site was verified here.
clinical_evidence: K220177 cleared the Magnus Neuromodulation System with SAINT technology in 2022 for adults with major depressive disorder who had not improved satisfactorily with prior antidepressant medication in the current episode. The early double-blind trial randomized 29 participants (14 active, 15 sham). Its size and follow-up constrain generalization. Manufacturer comparisons with remission percentages from unrelated treatments do not substitute for a head-to-head randomized study.
summary: A relatively clear university-to-company IP story, strengthened by named patents. Local product access and a fully verified payment pathway are less straightforward.
london_summary: No licensed Magnus SAINT site in London was verified. A clinic’s use of accelerated TMS alone does not establish SAINT use.

name: Exablate Neuro
description: Exablate Neuro uses focused ultrasound to make a small, controlled lesion in a brain target involved in a movement disorder. An array around the head directs ultrasound energy through the skull. At the focus, sufficient energy produces heating and tissue ablation. There is no implanted stimulation generator left behind.

MRI is used to plan the target and monitor the treatment, including temperature changes. The team can assess symptoms and side effects during the procedure while adjusting the delivered energy. In essential-tremor treatment, the aim is to reduce disabling tremor by interrupting activity in a selected circuit. This is permanent lesion treatment, rather than reversible electrical stimulation or the non-ablative ultrasound approaches being researched elsewhere.

The practical case includes more than the ultrasound device. It depends on a suitable MRI facility, skull/patient eligibility, specialist staff, treatment time and follow-up. These requirements affect who can benefit and the cost per treated patient. Essential tremor provides a more manageable topic than combining every indication and later bilateral-treatment expansion into one case.
stage: The original US brain indication was approved in 2016 for selected medication-refractory essential-tremor patients. Exact ExAblate equipment is documented in a London clinical paper, and UCLH publishes a relevant service route. Later indications require their own records.
clinical_evidence: The original US PMA (2016) concerns unilateral thalamotomy for medication-refractory essential tremor in adults meeting its label criteria. Later Parkinson’s and bilateral indications are separate regulatory events. A 2025 UCL/NHNN methods paper explicitly reports ExAblate Neuro equipment in London, providing stronger local evidence than a generic focused-ultrasound service description.
summary: A clear clinical and UK-payment starting point with a direct London team. Early development funding remains a harder section.

name: ARC-EX System
description: ARC-EX is an external spinal cord stimulation system used alongside rehabilitation to improve hand sensation and strength after selected cervical spinal cord injuries. Electrodes sit on the skin and connect to a programmable stimulator. It acts on spinal pathways rather than directly on the brain. It does not require a surgically implanted electrode and should be kept separate from ONWARD’s ARC-IM implant and ARC-BCI development programmes.

The treatment aims to make surviving neural pathways more responsive while a person practises useful movements. A rehabilitation professional selects the programme and combines stimulation with functional tasks such as reaching, grasping and manipulating objects. The product includes the stimulator, electrodes, control software and training/support workflow. The later home-use version lets a patient and, where needed, a helper use settings defined by the professional. It is not a stand-alone cure or a system that reads movement intentions from the brain.

For an engineering and business report, the useful unit of analysis is the whole rehabilitation pathway. Ask which patients can benefit, how many sessions and staff hours are needed, what equipment and consumables cost, and whether improvements remain useful outside sessions. These questions connect the technology to unmet need and payment. A nearby provider can explain that practical workflow, while company and university records are needed for the invention and financing history.
stage: A marketed device with original US De Novo authorization on 19 December 2024 (DEN240014) and a home-use extension cleared on 14 November 2025 (K251821). ONWARD announced CE marking in September 2025; its 2025 annual report says UK registration was completed. Exact-product UK provider listings are available. The original certificate/MHRA record and routine NHS commissioning were not independently verified here.
clinical_evidence: The 2024 Up-LIFT paper describes a prospective, single-arm, sequential study: two months of rehabilitation alone followed by two months with ARC-EX added. Of 65 enrolled participants, 60 completed; 43/60 (71.7%, rounded to 72%) met the predefined combined strength-and-function responder endpoint. The safety population was 64, with no device-related serious adverse events reported. The trial was not randomized or sham-controlled, so cumulative training, treatment order and expectation remain relevant limits. The smaller UK Pathfinder2 pilot provides community-workflow evidence; its abstract reports no significant group-level change in ISNCSCI motor/sensory scores despite improvements in selected functional measures. It should not be presented as universal neurological recovery.
summary: A useful addition for both public research and first-hand investigation: FDA records and a pivotal paper are accessible, and exact-device providers are near London. Product-specific patent mapping, earliest development spending and verified payment terms remain gaps.
london_summary: Neurokinex Hemel Hempstead and Gatwick are listed for ARC-EX and have a direct study connection, but are outside London. Spinal Research has a London office and a documented ARC-EX funding/access programme; it is not a treatment clinic. No central-London clinical user or London user-count comparison was verified.
